texts.preamble: Smt Manjula vs Sri Dayananda Sagar on 23 April, 2024 -1- Nc: 2024:Khc:16193 Mfa No. 3421 of 2017 C/W Mfa No. 3423 of 2017 Mfa No. 3424 of 2017 Mfa No. 4317 of 2017 Mfa No. 4318 of 2017 Mfa No. 4319 of 2017 In The High Court Of Karnataka At Bengaluru Dated This The 23Rd Day Of April, 2024
texts.facts: The Tribunal has awarded compensation in MVC No.509/16 against which the Insurance Company has filed MFA No.3421/2017 contending that claimant Nos. 5 and 6 are married daughters of deceased Ramaiah and thus, the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 Tribunal has erred in awarding compensation to them under `loss of estate' applying the multiplier system as in the case of loss of dependency at Rs.3,50,000/-. 5. In MVC No.510/2016 against which MFA No.3423/2018 is filed by the Insurer, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.30,96,160/- in favour of claimants 1 to 4 who are wife and children of deceased Ganesh, whereas, in MVC No.511/2016 against which MFA No.3424/2017, the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.1,70,000/- in favour of Mater Manoj-claimant/injured. MVC No.509/2016 was filed by Claimant No.5 Nagamma and claimant No.6 Anitha on account of death of their father Ramaiah and MVC No.510/2016 was filed by claimants being the wife and children of deceased Ganesh. MVC No.511/2016 was filed by claimant himself i.e. Master Manoj who sustained injuries on account accident that occurred on 28.12.2015. - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 7. The brief and relevant facts of the case of the claimants are as under: On 28.12.2015 at about 4.30 p.m. when the deceased Ganesh was riding Bajaj Chetak Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-S-6889 and his father Ramaiah was pillion rider along with his sister's minor son Master Manoj who were proceeding from Channena Agrahara to Anekal on account of ill-health of minor child- Manoj. When they were proceeding to Anekal near, Samandur Gate on Anekal-Hosur Road at that time, a bus bearing Regn.No.KA-01-C-3311 came from opposite direction from Anekal to Hosur in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle which Ganesh was riding. As a result, Ganesh, Ramaiah and Master Manoj fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 8. Immediately after the accident, the injured were shifted to Government Hospital, Anekal. But, the doctors declared Ganesh and Ramaiah brought dead and given - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 treatment to Master Manoj who sustained injuries in the accident. 9. The claimants filed petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 on the ground that the claimant nos.5 and 6 are none other than the daughters of deceased Ramaiah and the claimants in MVC No.510/2016 contended that claimant no.1 is wife of Ganesh, claimant nos. 2 and 3 are his daughters and claimant no.4 is the son of Ganesh. 10. The claimants have taken a contention that Ramaiah was aged about 58 years and was doing coolie work and also the milk vending business and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month. In MVC 510/2016, the claimants contended that Ganesh was aged about 36 years and he was working as driver in Madhura Garments, Marasur Gate, and earning Rs.15,000/- per month. 11. 12. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the claimants and respondent no.2-Insurance Company and perused the judgment and award of the tribunal. 13.
texts.arguments: . Learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that, the rider and pillion rider were majors who were succumbed to the injuries and the injured Boy Manoj was aged 14 years as on the date of accident. The rider of the motor cycle knew that he was riding Bajaj Chetak Scooter which was involved in the accident which is meant only for two adults and in extreme circumstances, a child could be accommodated. Considering the capacity of the vehicle, three grown up adults could not have traveled on Bajaj Chetak Scooter. That itself is sufficient ground for cause of accident. When somebody is traveling on a small vehicle with more number of persons, that itself is a detriment to the rider to ride the vehicle smoothly by following all the traffic rules. Therefore, in the fact situation, when the rider of the motorcycle has taken responsibility of taking two pillion riders on such a small vehicle, the rider of the vehicle should have been more cautious - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 in riding the motor cycle. It is needless to say that the accident took place in such a way that all the three persons on the scooter were grievously injured and out of them two were succumbed to the injuries. Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175811366/ 12 15. Therefore, the learned counsel contended that inspite of the fact that they knew about it that they have travelled on the said motorcycle putting their life into risk as well as the life of other road users to the risk, whereby, contributing to the cause of accident, have caused accident which is a matter of serious concerned. 16. Further, it is contended that, the very rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle itself is an offence which is punishable under the provisions of MV Act, inasmuch as, more than two persons travelling on the motorcycle, not being permissible. 28. In view of law laid down by the Supreme court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., vs. Nanu Ram @ Churu Ram and others1, claimant nos. 5 and 6 being the daughters of deceased Ramaiah, are entitled to (2017) 16 SCC 680 - 24 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of loss of parental consortium with 10% escalation which works out to Rs.44,000/- each and for two daughters, it will be Rs.88,000/- under the head `Loss of Parental Consortium'. Learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant sustained two grievous injuries and there is fracture of shaft of femur. Insofar as, rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, the learned counsel for the Insurer vehemently argued to reduce the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% contending that the same is on the higher side. In the decision rendered by this Court in MFA - 31 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 No.5896/2018 C/w.MFA Nos.4444 in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others vs. Venkateshan V and others wherein a similar question arose with regard to awarding of interest,
